name: Vendakkai Mandi

ingredients.name: okra, dried and cut into 4 cm pieces

steps: Rinse uncooked rice in clean water and reserve 450 ml of the cloudy second wash. Soak tamarind pulp in 120 ml warm water for 10 minutes, squeeze and strain to make tangy tamarind water.

Wash okra and dry it completely before cutting into 4 cm pieces; moisture on the pods makes them slimy. Heat 25 ml sesame oil and sauté okra over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes until the cut edges are lightly seared. Remove.

Heat remaining oil in the same pan. Crackle mustard seeds, add curry leaves and shallots, and sauté 5 minutes until the shallots soften. Add tomato, turmeric and chilli powder; cook until the tomato breaks down.
Pour in tamarind water and simmer 5 minutes to remove its raw taste. Add the reserved rice-washing water and salt, bring to a gentle simmer, then return the okra.
Cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes until the okra is tender and the rice-water gravy is slightly thickened but still spoonable. Rest 5 minutes and serve with steamed rice; avoid over-stirring the okra.
tips: Mandi means the cloudy water from washing rice; it gives this Chettinad tamarind-okra curry its characteristic light body.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
